Dignity Denied

By: Sibusisiwe Buthelezi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The City of Ekurhuleni fails the most vulnerable of our society

Unique Selling Point:
Accountability interview

Summary:
Last year, the City of Ekurhuleni was among the municipalities that received a tongue lashing from President Cyril Ramaphosa for failing to utilise the yearly budget allocated to them by National Treasury. The City returned R9,5 million that had been budgeted for infrastructure maintenance and repairs for city-run buildings.
The irony however, is that at least five city-run retirement villages could have benefitted from the money that was returned. Presidentia, Rusoord, Markville, Tweedy Park and Silver Krone are all retirement villages that fall under the City of Ekurhuleni. Another thing they all have in common is that they are falling apart and have been so as far back as 2021.
Residents are drowning in sewerage as burst pipes are not being attended to by the city. People who are in their 80s and 90s take cold showers because the geysers are not working. Sinks and toilets are broken, roofs are leaking, it’s just a nightmare and the elderly can do nothing about it without city intervention.
Worse still, despite there being a budget allocated for security at these facilities, the city has decided not to deploy any security. That has resulted in robbers targeting the place and strangling residents nearly to death in the process of robbing them of their belongings. The poor grannies and grandpas live in constant fear and have to take shifts falling asleep because they are worried that if they all sleep at the same time, they will be robbed again.
This is a story about government failing the most vulnerable of our society and both the Department of Human Settlements and the City of Ekurhuleni will be held accountable.
The residents have also previously reported their concerns to the Human Rights Commission, so they will also add a voice to the piece.
An organization called Serenity Senior Services has also been trying to get both the City and the Department to act. They will also add a voice to the piece.

Press Release:


Dignity Denied
Broken homes, sewage leaks, and no security: this is how inhabitants of government-run retirement homes live, while the City returns millions budgeted for maintenance and repairs, unspent. Volunteers try to stem the tide of overgrown vegetation and sewage while elderly residents endure cold showers, sleep under leaking roofs, and fear becoming targets of violent crime. Where is the municipality responsible for ensuring dignity in its citizens’ final years?
Producer: Sebe Buthelezi | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:


(Govan)- The bachelor section of Presidentia Retirement Village in Springs, Gauteng, is where 76-year-old Margaret Botha calls home.
(Govan)- It’s one of several facilities run by the City of Ekurhuleni.
(Govan)- She moved here eight years ago, after her husband died.
(Govan)- Since then, her health has deteriorated.
(Margaret Botha)- I’ve got a back problem and I’ve got a broken shoulder which won’t heal due to my osteoporosis.
(Govan)- A simple task, like bathing, has become nearly impossible, but after having a shower installed, she was summoned by a City official.
(Margaret Botha)- So she said if you have taken your bath out of your bathroom I can have you up for vandalisation.
(Govan)- It was a rare moment of official interest in Presidentia, where Margeret still lives in unsatisfactory conditions.
(Margaret Botha)- I’ve got a leak on my roof over my bed and I’ve lived here 8 years.
(Govan)- Margaret panics at the prospect of rain.
(Margaret Botha)- When I see storm clouds gathering, I run for my towels and I stack them all over the pillow on my bed because I know exactly where the leak is going to come in.
(Govan)- Despite repeated complaints to the city, nothing has been fixed.
(Govan)- Presidentia is one of 25 Affordable Pensioner’s Housing facilities run by the City.
(Govan)- Rents start from R279 per month.
(Govan)- In exchange, residents expect maintenance and basic services to be provided.
(Govan)- The community of Springs is stepping in to rescue the dignity of the elderly people living in this city-run retirement village. Because residents say, the municipality doesn’t care and is refusing to pay for maintenance.
(Govan)- In the last financial year, close to R10 million earmarked for infrastructure in the City of Ekurhuleni, encompassing most of Joburg’s East Rand, went unspent and was returned to the Treasury.
(Govan)- It was money that could have been used to protect the Metro’s most vulnerable but, instead, it gathered dust in a bank.
(Govan)- A few doors down from Margaret, another Presidentia resident is also dealing with the consequences of municipal incompetence.
(Ann Supra)- This is my last destination… you know… my last place to live.
(Govan)- At 77, Ann Supra says she doesn’t need much but guaranteed safety.
(Ann Supra)- When I heard that little alarm scream, I knew they opened that door.
(Ann Supra)- I just saw a light in my lounge now, I jumped up and the two of them were standing here.
(Govan)- She was trapped.
(Ann Supra)- They hit me here and I went like that because they wanted to hit my head. And my arms were blue, blue, blue, blue, blue.
(Govan)- After beating her, they made off with her TV and jewelry box.
(Govan)- The break-in was possible because the City hasn’t assigned security to Presidentia.
(Govan)- In recent months, Ekurhuleni has been thrust into the spotlight by revelations at the Madlanga Commission into allegations of criminality and interference in the SAPS.
(Govan)- Testimony has pointed to irregular contracts, weak oversight and the possible misuse of public funds.
(Govan)- And the impacts aren’t limited to policing. While easy to dismiss as insignificant, it seems the daily lives of people like Margaret and Ann are also affected, because the claims at Madlanga suggest a broader pattern of mismanagement in the City.
(Dorothy Oberholzer)- My geyser doesn’t work since I moved in.
(Govan)- In Brakpan, another pensioner’s village known as Tweedy Park is plagued by the City’s failures.
(Govan)- For nearly a year, Dorothy Oberholzer has lived without hot water.
(Dorothy Oberholzer)- They cut all the pipes down and bent it.
(Govan)- Yeah but this pipe is cut, it needs to be replaced.
(Dorothy Oberholzer)- Yeah.
(Govan)- Whose job is that?
(Dorothy Oberholzer- Subtitle)- The people from the municipality.
(Govan)- So the municipality destroyed it and they’re not fixing it.
(Dorothy Oberholzer)- No. But why is it taking so long.
(Govan)- In the 2024/25 financial year, R100 thousand was allocated to the upkeep of Tweedy Park.
(Govan)- According to municipal records, over R182 thousand was spent on maintenance.
(Govan)- Despite that, Dorothy’s geyser still hasn’t been fixed.
(Dorothy Oberholzer- Subtitle)- I use a bucket in the bathroom, and I boil about three kettlesful of water. Then I wash myself, and then I boil some more water. And that’s what I have to do.
(Govan)- And at Markville, another City-run facility, the evidence of mismanagement continued stacking up.
(Govan)- We were told this state-of-the-art generator, bought in 2020, hasn’t been serviced in years. And there were other examples.
(Govan)- Like fire hydrants that hadn’t been changed in more than a decade.
(Govan)- So this one says 2015. That’s the last time it was checked. That’s what maintenance money should pay for.
(Maryka Ras)- I think it’s just a lack of leadership and a lack of management from the councils.
(Govan)- Maryka Ras runs an NGO called Serenity Senior Services that looks after the interests of the elderly.
(Maryka Ras)- They do receive funding for these units to maintain it and for the upkeeping of the units, it’s just a lack of applying that money to where it should be going to.
(Govan)- After speaking to the elderly, we asked the City of Ekurhuleni how they could possibly justify their lack of maintenance. So they agreed to an interview.
(Govan)- Mayoral Committee Member for Human Settlements, Ngkopotse Mekgwe, has been in office for just over a month.
(Govan)- Are you aware of the state of these retirement villages?
(Ngkopotse Mekgwe)- I’m actually quite privy to the status of those properties.
(Govan)- What do you think of it?
(Ngkopotse Mekgwe)- At this point I am quite appeased, suffice to mention that perhaps we can also do better in some respects, especially on issues of plumbing specifically and issues of security.
(Govan)- You say your department is responsible for the maintenance of these properties. What kind of maintenance?
(Ngkopotse Mekgwe)- Maintenance in all respects, especially externally, the upkeep of the property, grass cutting, pruning of trees, obviously ensuring that the property externally is also clean.
(Govan)- But many would disagree.
(Maryka Ras)- No, the retirement village isn’t being maintained by Ekurhuleni at the moment, it’s the community that’s making a change in the retirement village at the moment.
(Govan)- Two years ago, Maryka’s NGO started getting volunteers to help with maintenance at Presidentia.
(Maryka Ras)- We have recorded all the leaks that are here and it’s plus minus 30 leaks.
(Govan)- 30 leaks at Presidentia alone?
(Maryka Ras)- We’ve submitted it to the council, they come out and take pictures of the ones we’ve reported but it’s never been repaired.
(Govan)- When we first entered Presidentia, there wasn’t a single council worker in sight. The only work being done was by grasscutters, who residents pay out of their own pockets.
(Govan)- But as we set up our cameras, council workers started appearing and began raking the leaves.
(Govan)- The municipality last year gave back R9.5 million which was meant for maintenance of various properties across the city. Why did you give the money back and why the maintenance is not being done?
(Ngkopotse Mekgwe)- Ok. There’s quite a misconception in terms of why the money was returned back to the Treasury.
(Govan)- Mekgwe claims the money wasn’t solely for his department.
(Govan)- Was any of that money meant for the maintenance of the retirement villages?
(Ngkopotse Mekgwe)- There is a portion of money that was apportioned for the maintenance of these residences.
(Govan)- Was any of the money spent on the maintenance of those residences?
(Ngkopotse Mekgwe)- There was, but not significant amounts were spent.
(Govan)- The MMC told us that contractors have been appointed, and that the concerns of residents would be addressed soon, including the unserviced fire hydrants which he agreed are a hazard.
(Govan)- But Margaret says she’s heard it all before.
(Margaret Botha)- I just sat in my car and cried.
(Govan)- It’s no way to live.
(Margaret Botha)- It’s no way to end your last chapter.
